name: Paneer Bhuna Masala
steps: Heat oil and half the ghee in a wide heavy pan. Add cumin; when fragrant, cook onions over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until deeply golden, stirring often.

Add ginger-garlic paste, coriander, chili and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute, then add tomatoes and 5 g salt. Cook uncovered for 12–15 minutes, pressing tomatoes down until the masala thickens and fat begins to separate.
Add water in three small splashes, frying the masala back down after each addition. This repeated bhuna step builds a dark, clingy sauce rather than a thin gravy.
In a separate pan heat the remaining ghee. Toss capsicum for 2 minutes, add paneer and sear gently for 2 minutes so the edges colour without becoming rubbery.
Fold the paneer and capsicum into the reduced masala with remaining salt and crushed kasuri methi. Cover and simmer 4 minutes, then serve hot with roti.
tips: Do not add all the water at once; the repeated frying after each splash is what makes this a bhuna masala.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
